questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to choose something within Europe so that I wouldn't be to far away from friends and family. At the same time it was important to me that the courses at the host university were taught in English so that no matter my level of competence in the local language I would still be able to learn. Finally I thought this to be a great idea to learn a new language and I already know a little bit of German so it would be the easiest language for me to learn so I decided that I wanted to got to a German speaking country. It also had to be a pretty big city since I wanted to go to a place where a lot of different stuff was happening. Because of all these factors I ended up choosing to go to Berlin.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found that Frei Universität had excellent orientation with both tours of the campus and an introduction the to the IT system that they use. The people studying in the physics department even got a separate tour only for us that really showed us the physics building.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During that tour which was on one of the first days of the semester the Erasmus contact person in Berlin sat us international students down and explain how to sign up of courses and other practical stuff.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was moderately difficult to find of campus housing. I got a mail which told us that there where certain dorm rooms we could sign up for. But because there are a very limited number of spots so you had to be really fast. I heard that they all got taking under 2 minutes so you really had to be ready the the right time to fil out the form.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living of campus is great since Frei Universität is a bit out side the city so most of campus accommodation will be closer to the city center than the university. Also I don't think there even is on campus accommodation at  Frei Universität.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Halbauer Weg Studenten Wohnheim which I lived at was fairly run down, but it was very cheap.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: To register for courses at Frei Universität you have to log into a system called Campus management and press that An-/Abmeldung button. Then make sure that you check the drop down menu, the system won't show all available courses as the default setting. Then it is as simple as press abmeldung. I think it's a little pencil icon, but i want quite remember.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: During the campus tour the student showing us around showed us how to do it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: For me it wasn't a problem because non of the courses I wanted had a participant limit. But from what I heard almost everybody gets the courses that they want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check the time tables. It's not like Copenhagen where we have 3 time slots that courses can be in. At Frei Universität the course can essentially be at any time, so it is easy to sign up for classes that have overlapping classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses where about the same level of difficulty as the ones in Copenhagen. Like in Copenhagen I had courses of varying difficulty from pretty relaxed to very difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The course structure was slightly different than back home and it was slightly different for the different courses. For all of them there was a bigger emphasis on participation during the semester. In all courses I had we had weekly assignments and the be able to attend the exam you had to get 50% over all the assignments. Some differences were course specific.

QFT: Here the exercise class work differently than in Copenhagen. I'm use to that when you show up the the exercise class mostly you do the exercises there. In QFT at Frei Universität the only exercises were the hand-in/home/assignments. So in the exercise class instead having the possibilities of working on them and asking the TA. The TA would go through last weeks assignment and get students to go through some of the problems.

Relativistic Particles in Condensed Matter: In this course the lectures and exercises were back to back so instead of having first two hours of lecture and the 2 hours of exercises the lecturer Maxim mixed them. So he would teach for 30 minutes than give us some exercises that we would do for a bit and then we would lecture for a bit again going back and forth.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
A pre-semester German course (Vorkurs)
Quantum Field Theory (QFT)
Methods in Molecular Simulation (MMS)
Relativistic Particles in Condensed Matter

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If future exchange students want to learn German the Vorkurs is an excellent opportunity for that. It is also where I met some of my closest friends during the exchange.
Quantum Field Theory is a hard course with a high work load, but it is also very good. The professor (Felix von Oppen) is good and you learn a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didn't really have any unexpected costs. The only thing I can think of is that I had to dry clean that bed cover before I left my dorm.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Things were generally cheaper. Especially if you avoid the touristy parts of the city stuff like beers, drinks and food gets significantly cheaper than in Copenhagen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a whole host of sports that students can sign up for and they only cost around 40 euros per semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I have thoroughly enjoyed exploring Berlins night life. The amount of unique and interesting bars and clubs is like no where else I've ever been. During the day one can walk around Kreuzberg and Neukölln which are some very interesting neighbourhoods. If the weather is for it there are several beaches along the lakes out west of the city that I would definitely recommend. Finally there is essential an unlimited amount of museum of every conceivable topic. One could go to a museum every weekend and you won't be close to getting through all of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In the weekends I would recommend everything I have written above and also there are a lot of parks in Berlin like Tiergarten where you can just hang out and drink a beer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture is very easy to a just to. The German culture is almost the same as the Danish one

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not much I mostly socialized with other international students. The one German student I did regularly talk to was a guy I had courses with so approaching then in the breaks during courses would be my best advice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There isn't anything that was challenging. The only thing that was a bit annoying is that that they are so cash reliant so you have to get used to always have cash on you.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I think the part that I appreciated the most is a Berlin specific thing, and that is the diversity of types of people that would will see walking around Berlin is like no where else.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you want a spot in a dorm you have to be ready and fast.
2. Take the German Vorkurs. It is a great way to make a lot of international friends that will stick through the semester.
3. Don't sign up for to much. Have some free time to just do stuff that comes up. You don't need a completely filled calendar.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think there's anything else that I haven't already covered in another box.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends from all over the world and knowing that if I ever visit their city I have a place to stay.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: One of the big challenges for me was finding courses that didn't overlap and in the end I even ended up having courses that overlapped and I couldn't attend every class.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
